w10_P4_002940: A cable works record ends with one number in joules. A reel of mass 36 kg is unwound at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 1x between x = 0 and x = 4. The energy the moving reel carries is the raw reading, from which 17 J is subtracted for the brake band. Four reels run per stand, and the works has 7 stands. A 65 L lubricant tank serves the stand and is not involved. What number ends the record, in J?
w10_P4_002943: A press shop certificate carries one figure in kilonewtons. A die block of mass 153 kg is accelerated on the bolster at a rate, in metres per second squared, worked out as 3 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 11. The drive must supply the force that gives the block that acceleration. Nine blocks work a press, and the shop has 10 presses. The shop total is finally written in kilonewtons. A 30 L quench bath stands beside the press and is not involved. What figure is on the certificate, in kN?
w10_P4_002944: A lift-testing bench drives a mass of 68 kg along a rail. The control curve is y = 5x^3 - 3x^2, and the acceleration applied to that mass, in metres per second squared, is the slope of the curve at x = 1. The drive must supply the force that gives the mass that acceleration, and the log records it in kilonewtons. Four rails run per bench, and the laboratory has 4 benches. A 12 L coolant bottle sits under the bench and takes no part. What is the laboratory total, in kN?
w10_P4_002945: A rolling mill report ends with one number in kilonewtons. A slab of mass 167 kg is accelerated on the table at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 5x^2 + 1x between x = 1 and x = 3. The rollers must supply the force that gives the slab that acceleration, and the report writes that force in kilonewtons. Eight slabs run per table, 11 tables run per mill, and the group has 11 identical mills. What number ends the report, in kN?
w10_P4_002951: A nursery groups two deliveries of 70 and 268 identical seedling trays into equal full racks, using the largest rack size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley of mass 105 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that rack size. Four trolleys work the glasshouse, so the house force is 4 times the corrected single-trolley value, and 12 N of door spring load is added to it. The result is written in kilonewtons. A 150 L irrigation butt stands at the end of the house and is not involved. What is the house figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002959: A drop-test summary ends with one number in kilojoules. The control curve is y = 4x^3 - 1x^2, and the slope of that curve at x = 1 is found first; multiplying that slope by 7 gives the impact speed, in metres per second, of the test mass. That mass has a plate reading 27000 g, and the energy it carries at that speed is the base value. Three drops make a run, so the run energy is 3 times the base value, and the summary writes that in kilojoules. To the record 18 is then added, in those same kilojoule units, as the rig allowance. What number ends the summary, in kJ?
w10_P4_002963: A drone test bench accelerates a payload whose mass plate reads 3000 g at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. The arm must supply the force that gives that payload that acceleration, and the log records that force in kilonewtons. Four arms carry identical payloads, so the airframe figure is 4 times the record. To that figure 8 is then added, in those same kilonewton units, as the frame allowance. What does the log show, in kN?
w10_P4_002964: A shot-put rig throws a weight whose mass plate reads 16000 g. Its release speed, in metres per second, is found by writing out k^2 for k running from 1 to 5 and adding the five values together. The energy the moving weight carries is the base value. From that total 20 J is subtracted for the catch net and then 15 J for the release gate, and 12 J is finally added for the spring return. The throwing circle is 3 m across, which is not needed. What is the session figure, in J?
w10_P4_002968: A rescue-training report ends with one number in kilojoules. A dummy of mass 36 kg slides at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the slope of the curve y = 1x^3 - 4x^2 at x = 3. w10_P4_002970: A trebuchet club launches a stone whose mass plate reads 15000 g. w10_P4_002972: A ropeway report ends with one number in newtons. A gondola of mass 141 kg is accelerated on the haul line. w10_P4_002975: An orchard groups two pickings of 306 and 82 identical crates into equal full stacks, using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. w10_P4_002997: A postal depot rolls a mail cage whose mass plate reads 5000 g along the floor. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. w10_P4_003002: A gallery groups two consignments of 154 and 43 identical frames into equal full crates, using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. w10_P4_003004: A canal lift record ends with one number in kilojoules. A caisson trolley of mass 46 kg moves at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. w10_P4_003028: A warehouse sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons.
